[THOUGHT]  
The clinical presentation is classic for Hirschsprung disease (HD): infantile onset of functional intestinal obstruction with constipation, feeding refusal, irritability, and abdominal tenderness — all consistent with distal colonic aganglionosis. The imaging findings are highly specific: absent rectal gas on abdominal X-ray reflects failure of gas to enter the aganglionic rectum, and the barium enema demonstrates a transition zone — the hallmark radiographic sign of HD, representing the abrupt junction between the dilated, ganglionated proximal colon and the narrow, aganglionic distal segment. The recommendation to avoid laxatives/enemas and to monitor for HAEC further underscores the diagnostic suspicion, as these are evidence-based precautions in HD. No contradictory findings are present (e.g., no evidence of mechanical obstruction from atresia or volvulus, no metabolic derangements, no signs of sepsis or systemic inflammation that would point away from HD). While rectal biopsy remains required for confirmation, the constellation of age, symptoms, and *two complementary, characteristic imaging findings* makes HD the single most likely diagnosis — not just “suspected,” but *diagnostically probable* pending histopathology.

[EVIDENCE]  
• Infantile presentation with chronic constipation/obstruction symptoms (feeding refusal, irritability, abdominal tenderness)  
• Abdominal X-ray shows dilated bowel loops and absent rectal gas  
• Barium enema reveals a transition zone in the distal colon  
• Clinical impression explicitly states “highly suspicious for Hirschsprung disease” based on the above  
• Recommendation to avoid enemas/laxatives due to HAEC risk — a complication unique to Hirschsprung disease  

[GAPS]  
• Absence of rectal biopsy result (required for definitive histopathologic confirmation of aganglionosis)  
• No mention of acetylcholinesterase staining or calretinin immunohistochemistry results (ancillary tests used to support biopsy interpretation)  
• No details on anorectal manometry (though not required for diagnosis in infants, it can provide supportive functional evidence)  

[DIAGNOSIS]  
Hirschsprung disease
